# `endpoints/webhook-without-signature`: Webhook endpoint does not verify the sender

<!-- Generated by `npm run docs:rules` from the rule metadata in src/rules/. Edit only the
     hand:* regions here; everything else comes from the rule and is overwritten. -->

| Family    | Default severity | GitHub security-severity | CWE                                                                                                                                                                                |
| --------- | ---------------- | ------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| endpoints | high             | 8.0                      | [CWE-345](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/345.html), [CWE-347](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/347.html), [CWE-306](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/306.html) |

Individual findings can have a lower or higher severity than the default, and each has a
confidence (high, medium or low). Both are explained below.

## What it detects

<!-- hand:detects -->

Route handlers, API routes and Express/Fastify routes whose path marks them as webhook
receivers (a `webhook`, `webhooks` or `hooks` segment, or `webhook` anywhere in the path) and
that verify no signature or shared secret. Signature checks are recognised from provider
SDKs and common helpers: `stripe.webhooks.constructEvent`, Svix / `webhooks.verify`,
`verifySignature…`, `verifyWebhook…`, `validateRequest` (Twilio), `isValidSignature`, and HMAC
comparison with `crypto.timingSafeEqual`. Receivers that also modify data are reported
with a stronger message. Server actions are never treated as webhooks.

<!-- /hand:detects -->

## Why it matters

Webhook URLs are public and easy to guess (/api/webhooks/stripe). Without verifying the provider's signature (or a shared secret), anyone can POST a fake "payment succeeded" or "user created" event and your handler will act on it. Session-based auth does not apply here: the sender must be authenticated by signature.

## Messages

What a finding from this rule says (parameters in braces):

- {endpoint} looks like a webhook receiver but verifies no signature or shared secret.
- {endpoint} is a webhook receiver that modifies data ({api}) without verifying the sender's signature: anyone can forge events.

## How to fix

Verify the signature over the raw request body with the provider SDK (stripe.webhooks.constructEvent, svix Webhook.verify, @octokit/webhooks verify) or an HMAC with crypto.timingSafeEqual, and reject unsigned or stale events before touching data. If a gateway verifies signatures for you, suppress this finding with that reason.

### Vulnerable

```ts
export async function POST(req: Request) {
  const event = await req.json(); // anyone can send this
  if (event.type === 'checkout.session.completed') await markPaid(event.data.object.id);
}
```

### Fixed

```ts
export async function POST(req: Request) {
  const event = stripe.webhooks.constructEvent(
    await req.text(), // raw body, not JSON-parsed
    req.headers.get('stripe-signature')!,
    process.env.STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET!,
  ); // throws on a bad signature
  if (event.type === 'checkout.session.completed') await markPaid(event.data.object.id);
}
```

## False positives and limitations

<!-- hand:false-positives -->

- **Signature checks in a helper** are followed one level. Deeper helpers or a check in a
  package are not seen. Suppress with the reason, or call the check in the handler.
- **Verification by a gateway** (some platforms verify webhook signatures before your code
  runs) is invisible. Suppress with that reason.
- **Endpoints named "webhook" that are not receivers** (for example a UI route that lists
  webhooks): suppress with the reason.
- **Limitations:** replay protection (timestamp checks) is not verified.

<!-- /hand:false-positives -->

## How to suppress

Only suppress a finding after confirming it is safe. Put the directive on the line above
the reported line (or use `vibeguard-ignore-line` on the line itself, or
`vibeguard-ignore-file` anywhere in the file). The reason is required: a directive without
one suppresses nothing and is reported.

```ts
// vibeguard-ignore-next-line endpoints/webhook-without-signature -- explain why this is safe (at least 10 characters)
<the line VibeGuard reported>
```

Use the comment syntax of the file: `//` or `/* */` in code, `#` in `.env` and YAML
files, `--` in SQL.

To turn the rule off or change its severity for the whole project, use `.vibeguard.yml`:

```yaml
version: 1
rules:
  endpoints/webhook-without-signature: off # or: { severity: low }
```

See [configuration](../../configuration.md) and
[ADR-0004](../../adr/0004-suppression-design.md).

## CWE

- [CWE-345](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/345.html): Insufficient Verification of Data Authenticity
- [CWE-347](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/347.html): Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature
- [CWE-306](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/306.html): Missing Authentication for Critical Function
